metadata.title: Email Identity

props.name: capability
props.remarks: Business capability for ensuring correct, defensible, and non-deceptive use of sender identity in institutional email systems.

props.name: technology-domain
props.remarks: Email address namespaces, shared mailboxes, aliases, delegation mechanisms, and identity verification controls.

props.name: architecture-pattern
props.remarks: Pattern for governing sender identity, delegation, and impersonation resistance in email environments.

props.name: depends-on
props.remarks: Email identity trust depends on baseline email transport, routing, and identity binding provided by Email Core.

props.name: data-object
props.remarks: Sender identity attributes and mailbox bindings as managed institutional information objects.

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: Referenced for trustworthy email guidance related to sender authentication, identity policy, and impersonation prevention.

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: Referenced for guidance on secure handling of email identities and prevention of unauthorized use.

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: Referenced to emphasize email identity as a critical trust dependency whose misuse can cause cascading institutional impact.

metadata.remarks: Email Identity defines the trust properties required to ensure that sender identity claims in email are accurate, authorized, and resistant to impersonation. This pattern governs delegation, shared mailboxes, aliases, and external identity trust.

components.title: Authorized Sender Assertion
components.description: Ensures that only authorized identities may send email using a given sender address.

props.name: attack-technique
props.remarks: Abuse of valid email accounts to send unauthorized or deceptive messages.

props.name: attack-technique
props.remarks: Mailbox rule and delegation abuse to impersonate authorized senders.

props.name: defensive-technique
props.remarks: Enforcement of privileged access controls over delegated and service identities.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Email identity attributes are managed to prevent unauthorized use or alteration.
Identity assurance mechanisms support accurate attribution of email sender identities.
Email sending privileges are restricted to the least privilege necessary.

components.title: Delegation and Shared Mailbox Governance
components.description: Governs delegated email access and use of shared or functional mailboxes.

props.name: attack-technique
props.remarks: Creation or misuse of email accounts to impersonate legitimate senders.

props.name: attack-technique
props.remarks: Email content abuse following identity compromise or misdelegation.

props.name: defensive-technique
props.remarks: Hardening of shared and delegated identities to reduce impersonation risk.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Shared and delegated email accounts are explicitly provisioned, managed, and reviewed.
Access enforcement mechanisms restrict delegated email usage to authorized contexts.
Delegated email access follows the principle of least privilege.

components.title: Impersonation and Spoofing Resistance
components.description: Reduces the risk of deceptive or misleading sender identities in email communications.

props.name: attack-technique
props.remarks: Creation of malicious email accounts used for impersonation.

props.name: defensive-technique
props.remarks: Verification mechanisms that reduce the ability to register or use deceptive sender identities.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Mechanisms are in place to mitigate impersonation of email identities.
Email system design mitigates unauthorized identity claims and spoofing.
